components.name: Writing Field
components.description: Borderless serif surface for composing posts and comments.

narrative.overview: A feed that reads like a small publication with a face. Every post opens with a person and is set as a short published note in a serif reading face, over a quiet hairline list. Controls and labels stay in the system sans so that writing is the only thing that looks written.
keyCharacteristics: Serif (Literata) for post text, writing surfaces, the writing prompt, screen titles and display names; system sans for every control and label.
Hairline separators, no card boxes, no shadows.
Round avatar discs: lilac with two overlapping circles for anonymous, blue-tinted with an initial for known.
Line icons at one stroke weight (1.75).
Light and dark schemes with a shared role vocabulary.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: Blue means you can act on this or this is selected. It is never used as decoration.

rules.name: The Lilac Means Anonymous Rule
rules.body: Lilac appears only where an anonymous profile is speaking.

rules.name: The Words Carry Identity Rule
rules.body: Identity is always also stated as a text chip; colour is never the only signal.

rules.name: The Serif Is For Words People Wrote Rule
rules.body: Literata is for what a student writes or is prompted to write, plus screen titles and names; controls never use it.

rules.name: The Hairline Instead Of A Box Rule
rules.body: Separate content with a hairline, not a bordered card.

dos: Do open every post with a person: avatar, name, handle, time, identity chip.
Do set anything a student writes in Literata and every control in the system sans.
Do separate with hairlines and keep surfaces flat.
Do keep 44px targets and state identity as words.
Do keep icons to the one line style at 1.75 stroke.
donts: Don't wrap posts in outlined cards or lines of identical outlined buttons.
Don't use lilac for anything but anonymous identity.
Don't add shadows, gradients or decorative colour.
Don't use an icon alone to carry a state without an accessible label.
